answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks lose their edge when each identity must stake a refundable bond that vests slowly, the way water seeps through a sand dune rather than pooling instantly. Reputation then flows like nectar only to agents whose peers repeatedly attest to them across many epochs, so a swarm of fresh clones starts with none. Genuine standing accrues a distinct pigment of verified history that forgeries cannot cheaply paint on, making mass fake-identity creation economically ruinous.
